item.title: $5M Dream Home In North Beach Was Illegally Converted From Four Units; Board of Supes to Decide Its Fate
item.description: A family thought they had found a dream property in North Beach, a rare single-family home with a roof deck and four spacious bedrooms. But somewhere in its last couple of renovations, a previous owner did something they shouldn't have.

item.title: Feds Charge Big-Time NorCal Wine Distributor Execs In Pay-for-Placement Scheme at Stores Run By Safeway Owner
item.description: Safeway’s parent company Albertson’s has been taking wine shipments from a distributor whose former executives are accused of making elaborate bribes in exchange for prime placement on the grocery shelves.

item.title: How Live Nation's Antitrust Settlement Could Impact San Francisco Venues
item.description: Live Nation, the parent company of Ticketmaster, has now settled its antitrust case with the US Department of Justice, and as part of the settlement the company has said it will divest some of its exclusive agreements with venues.

item.title: Video: See the Drone Show That Followed Saturday's Chinese New Year Parade
item.description: After technical difficulties grounded the drones in 2025, a successful drone show lit up the sky over the Bay by SF's Embarcadero in celebration of the Year of the Horse.

item.title: Group to Protest Over Plan to Install 20 Acres of Astroturf at Crocker Amazon Park
item.description: Residents are protesting at FanFest Saturday over SF Rec and Park’s plan, in partnership with the Giants, to install 20 acres of artificial turf at Crocker Amazon Park to create five new baseball diamonds, which requires the removal of over 100 trees and the disruption of a vital green corridor.

item.title: Parking Citations Are Most Frequent In the FiDi, Marina, North Beach, and SoMa
item.description: Predictably, SF’s most ticketed neighborhoods see a mix of commercial, commuter, and tourist traffic along with heavier enforcement, including the Financial District, SoMa, the Marina, and North Beach, garnering the majority of citations for street-cleaning and expired meters.

item.title: Two Men Charged In Altercation With Mayor's Bodyguards In Tenderloin
item.description: The two Tenderloin denizens who got into a street scuffle last week with bodyguards assigned to Mayor Daniel Lurie have been charged and will be arraigned Tuesday.

item.title: Rep. Eric Swalwell Going to Bat for Deported Hayward Family of Three With Deaf Six-Year-Old Boy
item.description: ICE deported a six-year-old deaf boy from Hayward along with his mom and brother, but Eric Swalwell is trying to win the return of this family of three, and his staff did at least get the kid his hearing aids.

item.title: SFUSD Schoolkids Getting Five Extra Days of Class in June to Make Up for Strike
item.description: Kids missed a few days of instruction in last month's SFUSD teachers’ strike, but they’re going to make it up, because the school district submitted plans to extend the school year to June 10 instead of June 3.

item.title: Day Around the Bay: Attempted Murder Charge In Chinatown Stabbing
item.description: A 37-year-old man has been charged with attempted murder for a stabbing last week in Chinatown; the second victim has been ID'd in the Oakland bar shooting; and chaos has erupted in New York outside the mayor's residence.
